A non-zero `witness_quorum` below ⌊n/2⌋ + 1 stays refused. **A charter silent on `witness_quorum` is in witnessed mode off**, exactly as one declaring `0` — the reading [CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)'s forward-compatibility table already gives an absent member ("the lineage is unwitnessed for T6") — so every charter minted before rc6 keeps working unchanged, and witnessed mode is only ever on by an explicit, valid value; a substrate MUST NOT substitute an internal default. **`n` is the size of the witness directory in force for the head being judged** — the `witnesses[]` of the charter its parent carries (the parent-directory rule above), not of any later charter and not a count at the consumer's instant.

*Equivocation, in two tiers.* Two heads for one lineage that each meet the witness quorum are **equivocation**: the substrate MUST raise `hard_case:lineage_equivocation:{lineage_key_id}` ([CC 3.4.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)) carrying both digests and both cosignature sets, MUST NOT adopt a new head for that lineage until the adjudication plane rules — where, as for ledgers, equivocation is distinguished from honest stale-state recovery before anything is slashed — and no consumer may attach to a frozen lineage until then. The freeze suspends **head adoption only**: `withdraws`, `recants`, tombstones, `revoked_after` bounds and the halt latch are single-signer, head-independent rows and keep landing, so a compromised founder key that equivocates cannot use the freeze to hold its own revocation hostage (T4). A consumer already attached keeps its current state on its current head. A head that carries a signature valid under the lineage's quorum *at that head's instant* ([CC 2.6](part_2_the_grammar.md) `revoked_after` read-time rule) but does not descend from the lineage's witnessed head is a **fork attempt**, not equivocation: recorded once per `(lineage_key_id, fork point)` — the fork point being the nearest ancestor **on the witnessed chain**, so a chain of forks off a fork shares one point — as `hard_case:lineage_fork_attempt:{lineage_key_id}`, never cosigned, further attempts off the same point counted and not stored, and never freezing — a founder set revoked at head five can sign forks off head four forever, and none of them may freeze the honest lineage. A consumer that holds a witnessed head MUST refuse a competing head that is not witnessed, and MUST NOT silently adopt a first-seen fork; first-seen-wins is retired for witnessed lineages and unchanged for ordinary rooms. A founder roster recovering from its own restore re-syncs its head from the witness plane before it writes, exactly as a ledger owner does. The head a consumer needs inside T4a's attach window is *this* witnessed head: one object serves both rules.

**T7 — Liveness margin and the stalled state (MUST; [CIRISConstitution#120](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/120)).** The `infrastructure` conformance requirements above forbid `founder_only`, `unanimous` and bare `majority` so that no single founder can admit alone and no growable core needs all-N. Under [CC 4.4.3.4.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md)'s absolute-M reading that protection holds at founding and erodes with the first exit: three founders at `quorum:2/3` lose one and the two who remain must both sign, so from that instant any one of them stalls the root, and recovery routes through the same two. [CC 4.2.6](part_4_composition_governance.md) settles this for the accord family alone, with a live set and a floor-of-1 fire, and nothing there reaches an `infrastructure` community or any other conferring family.

*Scope.* T7 applies to every `infrastructure` community and to every conferring family as T6 defines it, and **not to the accord family (`humanity-accord`)**, whose liveness is [CC 4.2.6](part_4_composition_governance.md)'s and which T7 never evaluates; T8's `Rooted` evaluates this leg over the root community only, never over the family that conferred it. A `geographic` community evaluates over its current member set and needs no margin.

*One founder predicate.* Founder eligibility under *Infrastructure does not vote* — a `user` key with a ceremony-plane conferral, or a current holder of the conferring accord family — is **one predicate**, applied identically at admission, in the active founder set below, and in T8's standing verdict; a key that admission seats as founder and the fold does not count would leave the root born stalled. *The active founder set.* Founder *f* counts at instant *t* iff: *f* was seated as founder by the base row or an admitted widening whose `effective_at ≤ t`; no admitted revocation or `withdraws` of or by *f* has `effective_at ≤ t`; *t* < the effective `revoked_after` of *f*'s key (the minimum across its revocations, [CC 2.6](part_2_the_grammar.md)); and *f*'s `identity_type` **as read at its seating row** does not include `node` (*Infrastructure does not vote*) — a later key record that adds `node` is a resignation at that record's `asserted_at`, so no `node`-bearing seat ever moves a state by being one. Resignation and removal are one row kind at the fold; the grammar does not distinguish them here.

*Live and stalled.* A collective in scope with `consensus_protocol: quorum:M/N` — where `M ≥ 2`, `quorum:1/N` being non-conformant for the same reason `founder_only` is — is **live** while its active founder set holds at least **M + 1** signers and **stalled** when it holds M or fewer: at exactly M every remaining founder is a veto, below M no founder-quorum act is possible. Stalled is a **declared state**: the substrate that admitted the row whose `effective_at` moved the count — for a `revoked_after` crossing, the substrate that admitted the revocation row — MUST emit `hard_case:community_liveness_stalled:{community_key_id}` ([CC 3.4.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)) with its `event_id` keyed on that row, and `hard_case:community_liveness_restored:{community_key_id}` the same way on recovery; peers re-derive the verdict from the rows and do not emit, and between the two events any fold reproduces the state. A stalled root is **valid but non-admitting**, and *non-admitting* means exactly this: no roster widening or removal by the founders' count, and no ceremony-plane conferral by this roster, until the margin is restored. Everything else is unchanged — serve, vouch, manifest validity, score validity, single-key delegations under the charter's scope — and T4 holds: nothing detaches, no running node loses federation, and a node whose acceptance edge is written into `Stalled` is federated.

*Recovery.* Recovery is by the **conferring body**, never by the remaining founders lowering M (entrenchment, [CC 4.5.1.2](part_4_composition_governance.md)) and never by the members. Because the founders' count cannot admit the row that would restore it, a stalled roster admits **exactly one row kind without that count**: a widening whose only change is the addition of a **founder** seat for a key that carries a live ceremony-plane conferral from the collective's conferring family — `trust:confers:v1` under a co-scrub reaching that family's `consensus_protocol`, the same act that seated the original founders — and whose `identity_type` includes `user` and excludes `node`; the conferral's `scope` MUST name this collective's `community_key_id` (or `family_key_id`), so a key conferred as steward of one lineage cannot seat itself in every stalled lineage under the same family; the widening row is signed by the conferred key itself, and the conferral is its authority. The substrate verifies the conferral, not a founder count; the conferring body does not thereby sit in the quorum, it exercises the power that made the quorum. The residual is named rather than hidden: a conferring body that can both retire a founder (a revocation *of* a seat) and confer one can replace a stalled roster seat by seat, with no founder-count act — that is the power that founded the roster, held by the accord for `ciris-canonical`, and the membership-ceremony sentence above is amended accordingly. For `ciris-canonical`, whose founders are the accord holders themselves, a founder seat is lost when its holder leaves the accord roster ([CC 4.2.6](part_4_composition_governance.md)), and the recovery widening seats the replacement holder, who signs it. The exception is bounded the way a restore-only power is bounded: it can only *add* a conferred human founder, only while stalled, and can never remove a seat, change `M`, the protocol, the basis or the subkind — so it cannot be a seizure vector, and it removes the veto that #120 named rather than relocating it. For `ciris-canonical` this is the accord's co-scrub conferring a replacement steward founder.

*Founding and floors.* A collective in scope MUST be founded at **N ≥ M + 1** active human founders; founding at N = M is non-conformant. A charter or admission floor that *raises* the effective M — a strict-majority floor, or an unknown protocol read as unanimity ([CIRISPersist#927](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISPersist/issues/927)) — is itself a liveness reduction and MUST be refused at the founding row's admission and MUST NOT be applied at read time; the charter leg reads the protocol the row declares. Resignation stays one row: this rule does not slow an exit; it makes the exit's cost loud.

**T8 — The standing verdict is a state machine, and the machine is the normative object ([CIRISConstitution#121](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/121)).** T1–T7, [CC 3.3.9](part_3_the_namespace.md)'s stable-id current-state resolution, [CC 2.6.7](part_2_the_grammar.md)'s instant discipline and [CC 4.2.6](part_4_composition_governance.md)'s live set each fix one edge of the same question — *is this node rooted right now?* — and the rc5 review rounds found five instant-related corners of that question by reading code. Prose spread across seven rules cannot show that it has no sixth. The verdict is therefore stated once, as a function **V(rows, t)** an implementer can check and a model checker can exhaust: *t* is a signer-stamped instant, never the evaluating clock, and the [CC 2.6.7](part_2_the_grammar.md) skew rule gates T4a's attach refusal only, never V.

*States.* `Rooted` — a live conferral chain runs from the evaluating node's self-root (T1) through its own `trust:accepts:v1` edge (T3) to a root whose charter carries a pre-rotation recovery commitment and a scope set covering at least `infra:serve` and `infra:attest`, whose lineage has a current head under T6 (witnessed, or anchored out of band while witnessed mode is off), whose active founder set is live (T7, evaluated over the root only; satisfied by definition when the root is the accord family itself), and on which no halt has reached this node. Holder custody ([CC 4.2.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md)) is an admission gate at the seating row, never a leg of V — an attestation chain can lapse without a row, and V has no inputs but rows. `Stalled` — every leg of `Rooted` holds except the margin: valid and non-admitting (T7). `NotRooted` — otherwise, including: no acceptance edge; the edge, the charter or the community row withdrawn, recanted, tombstoned or past its effective `revoked_after`; the charter missing its recovery commitment or its scope; the head de-witnessed (its counted witnesses revoked before their `signed_at`, or the directory collapsed to non-independent keys); the halt latched; and, at attach time only, a head whose counted cosignatures are older than `attach_window_secs`, or a lineage frozen as equivocation (T4a, T6) — the freeze is an attach-time clause and never a leg of V for a node already attached.

*Inputs.* The lineage's heads and their cosignatures; the roster fold (seats, roles, `effective_at`s); `withdraws`, `recants`, tombstones and `revoked_after` bounds; each seat's `identity_type` at seating; the charter in force; the evaluating node's own acceptance edge and the `attached_head_digest` it names (an edge whose digest no longer verifies under (viii) is read as naming that head's nearest verifying ancestor, so T4 holds); the halt latch **as it reaches this node** ([CC 4.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md): a live accord edge at the halt's `asserted_at`); and *t*.

*Transitions.* Every transition is a row, or the crossing of an instant a row declares, and the machine names which moves which state: the acceptance edge written (`NotRooted → Rooted`, or `→ Stalled` by the margin at *t*); the edge deleted (`→ NotRooted`, one row, T3); the halt latched (`→ NotRooted`) and `accord:lifecycle:active` admitted (`→` the state the remaining legs give — an edge deleted during the halt stays deleted); a revocation, `withdraws` or `revoked_after` crossing that takes the active set to M or fewer (`Rooted → Stalled`); the T7 recovery widening restoring the margin (`Stalled → Rooted`); a new witnessed head that removes a leg — a charter re-scrub dropping the recovery commitment, a directory collapse — (`→ NotRooted`); a competing witnessed head (no transition for an attached node — the freeze is attach-time only — and nobody attaches); a `revoked_after` lowered below a head's `asserted_at` (see viii).

*What never happens — the invariants a model MUST prove.* (i) A seat whose `identity_type` at seating includes `node` never moves a state by its own signature. (ii) V(rows, *t*) is constant on every interval of *t* that contains no `effective_at` and no `revoked_after` of any row — a lapsed timer (drill staleness, an expired `attach_window_secs`, a missed `witness_cadence_secs`) never moves `Rooted` or `Stalled` to `NotRooted`. (iii) A `withdraws` or resignation never reaches behind the head's link instant: it removes the signer from every later *t* and from no earlier one; a key revocation reaches behind only through its `revoked_after` bound, per (viii). (iv) The edge-written transition is enabled only on a head whose counted cosignatures are fresh and at least `witness_quorum`: a stale or under-quorum head never yields `Rooted` on attach (a guard on the transition, with the served head as environment input). (v) A halt latched at *t₀* is `NotRooted` at every *t > t₀* until `accord:lifecycle:active`, whatever roster rows land between. (vi) Deleting the acceptance edge is sufficient for `NotRooted` from any state, and from `NotRooted` *for want of an edge* nothing but a new edge naming a head re-enters `Rooted` — no conferral, however strong its ceremony (a halt resumed, or a head re-witnessed, re-enters on the edge that never left). (vii) V(rows, *t*) is independent of the order in which the rows arrived — the fold commutes — so it is byte-equal on every node holding the same rows. (viii) A `revoked_after` lowered below a witnessed head's `asserted_at` is applied at read time, fail-closed, as [CC 2.6](part_2_the_grammar.md) says: for such a revocation *v* and head *h*, V(rows ∪ {*v*}, *t*) equals V over the rows with *h* and every head descending from *h* removed, for all *t* — the lineage's current head is the latest witnessed head that still verifies, and the signer leaves the active set from the bound onward. This is the one input that moves the verdict backward in instant order, and it is the intended one — witnessing records that the world saw a head; it does not make a compromised key's signature good.

*Evidence.* A mechanized model of this machine — TLA+ or Alloy, checked for (i)–(viii) over bounded founder sets and instant orderings, with the five rc5 review corners encoded as named invariants before any other property is added, so that the model begins by proving it would have caught what the reviewers caught — lives at `formal/trust_root/` in this repository and is a mechanized-evidence row at this decimal beside the `impl:` rows persist and server publish, under the tier the coherence-ratchet Lean rows and RATCHET's formal manifest already use ([CIRISConstitution#127](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/127)). Until it lands, this rule is a claim the Constitution makes, and the register says so.


## Section CC 4.2

## 4.2 `accord` — The HUMANITY_ACCORD constitutional layer

The federation is symmetric by design — every participant binds every other under the Recursive Golden Rule. The wire format carries exactly one asymmetry, and it points outward: humanity's right to halt the system. That asymmetry is keyed on a **slot**, not on the parties currently in it — per the [CC 1](part_1_foundation.md) reading rule, who holds the accord seats is an instance parameter, and anyone may instantiate this form and name their own occupants. What CC specifies is the slot; who fills it in the CIRIS mesh is [CC 4.2.3](#423-accord-holder--the-accord-holder-triple). This section specifies the slot. The asymmetry is **consent-scoped**: it reaches exactly those holding a live trust edge to the accord, and it dies when that edge is cut ([CC 4.2.1](#421-authority--authority-scope) reach, [CC 4.4.3.8](#4438-policy-direct--policy-a--direct-trust) un-trust). The humanity accord is *a* trust root, not *the* trust root; what it holds over those who root to it is an emergency brake they granted, not a power imposed on everyone.

### 4.2.1 `authority` — Authority scope

`HUMANITY_ACCORD` signatures are valid only on `EmergencyShutdown CONSTITUTIONAL` (`IncidentSeverity::INCIDENT_CONSTITUTIONAL = 5`), `accord:invoke:notify:{notify_id}`, `accord:invoke:drill:{drill_id}`, `accord:lifecycle:active`, the **canonical-conferral co-scrub** and the **pipeline-attest co-scrub** below, and the corresponding `FederationAnnouncement` priority `AccordCarrier`. Announcements of any other priority signed by accord-holder keys are rejected at admission (out of role). **Mesh-config authorship (normative — CIRISConstitution#57, ratified).** This enumeration's silence confers no authority; the mesh-config author is **the trust root, acting on the [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md) delegation plane** (`trust:confers:v1`), never the accord's ceremony plane — this scope isolation stands verbatim, and the trust edge is the subscription, inheriting the T3 one-row un-trust lever. Four rules bind: **(1) relieve-never-expand** — a `mesh_config` action MAY relieve or restrict and MUST NOT expand what flows; no key may cause a node to share more than its owner consented to; restrictions compose safely under plural authority and grants do not, so **most-restrictive-across-roots** is forced, not preferred. **(2) Closed key registry** — a config key naming no consumer processor MUST be refused at admission. **(3) Emergency relief is TTL-bounded** — threshold-1 on the announce carrier, TTL ≤ 72 h, not renewable back-to-back by the same holder; **durable** settings are earned by **quorum, never by having been exercised**: the root's own quorum MAY establish a durable setting directly (cold), or MAY ratify a held emergency's `payload_sha256` as a linked object — two routes to one authority. (The TTL of this rule attaches to *unilateralness*, per rule (4)'s own logic; a reading that admitted durability only via ratifying a prior unilateral act would make quorum weaker than a single threshold-1 holder and hand that holder agenda control over every durable setting the mesh can hold — CIRISConstitution#86, ruled.) **(4)** The halt asymmetry is deliberate: relief expires because it is unilateral; the halt carries no TTL because its exit is the named resumption. Federation-side authority cannot sign `AccordCarrier`; humanity-accord authority cannot sign anything else. **Wire-isolated AND scope-isolated.**

**Root conferral is in scope.** The enumeration admits a 2-of-3 accord co-scrub over a `canonical,node` registration envelope bearing `roles: ["infra:serve"]` — the ceremony that mints a **portable trust root** ([CC 4.4.3.8](#4438-policy-direct--policy-a--direct-trust)). Read without it, the clause forbids the accord from blessing the very primitive that creates a root. Scope isolation still does its real work: accord authority cannot reach the consent or licensure planes. It does **not** isolate the amendment plane — [CC 4.5.1](#451-amendment--amendment-process--federation-contribution--wa-quorum--1-of-6-sign-off) step 5 and its pre-maturity authority, and the [CC 4.5.1.2](#4512-meta-amendment--meta-amendment--entrenchment) entrenched 2-of-3 ratification, all name accord-holders. That reach is stated here rather than denied; per the [CC 1](part_1_foundation.md) reading rule it is a **default** of this instance — escaped by naming your own occupants — not a privilege requiring declaration. Root-minting is **not** an accord privilege — the identical ceremony under any other root's holders mints an equally valid root, and the CIRIS root is the shipped default, not a privileged one ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md): a default-plus-re-root is a federation). Conferral MUST NOT be relocated to a founder-quorum of an infrastructure community: that is circular at genesis — a community presupposes admission, which presupposes a root — and destroys portability.

**Blessing a build pipeline is in scope (normative — steward ruling 2026-10-01, [CIRISConstitution#137](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/137)).** The enumeration also admits a 2-of-3 accord co-scrub over a CI pipeline's key record whose scrub-signed envelope bears `roles: ["infra:attest"]` and nothing wider. It is the root-conferral ceremony applied to a second subject: the roster that confers a root's identity also says which pipelines may attest that root's builds, and a reader evaluates the pipeline's standing on that ceremony plane ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md) T2, [CC 3.1.2.1](part_3_the_namespace.md)). Three bounds hold. **(1)** The role is `infra:attest` — authority to *emit* build claims as the root's infrastructure — and it confers no right to be believed beyond what each reader's own trust in the root gives it ([CC 3.4.5.1](part_3_the_namespace.md)); a co-scrub bearing any other role on a pipeline record is out of role and refused. **(2)** A pipeline key is not a holder, a founder or a voter, and its record carries no seat. **(3)** It ends as any conferral on a key record ends: the conferring roster's revocation of the record, or the T3 un-trust of the root by the reader. Like root-minting, this is **not** an accord privilege: the identical co-scrub by any other root's conferring roster blesses that root's pipelines, and a root MAY instead bless a pipeline by a `trust:confers:v1` grant on the delegation plane. *Ratification status.* This paragraph amends the **entrenched** CC 4.2 surface ([CC 4.5.1.2](#4512-meta-amendment--meta-amendment--entrenchment)) by adding one enumerated use of the accord's signature. It is ratified by the **founder under the [CC 4.5.1](#451-amendment--amendment-process--federation-contribution--wa-quorum--1-of-6-sign-off) maturity gate**; post-maturity, a change to this enumeration requires the dedicated 2-of-3 entrenched accord ratification. It records the mechanism already in production (CIRISServer `/v1/accord/ci-key`; persist `is_infra_attest_effective`) and changes no signed bytes.

**Reach is consent-scoped (normative).** A `constitutional` halt binds exactly the nodes holding a **live `delegates_to(user → accord)`** at the invocation's `asserted_at`. The halt rides the same edge as everything else the accord confers and dies with it on un-trust ([CC 4.4.3.8](#4438-policy-direct--policy-a--direct-trust)); a node that never trusted the accord, or has already cut the edge, is simply not reached. Consumers MUST resolve reach against the edge set pinned at `asserted_at`, not at apply time: **exit is prospective, never retroactive.** Severing an edge *after* an invocation's `asserted_at` MUST NOT remove the severing node from that halt's reach — otherwise the halted party escapes by un-choosing at the instant the brake is pulled, and the consent was a preference rather than a binding. The complementary rule binds the accord: **pre-committed powers only, never act-then-ratify.** The accord's powers are exactly those enumerated here, over edges already held; any change *widening* accord reach (a charter amendment adding scopes) takes effect only after a published **severance window** — 72 h baseline, the [CC 4.2.6](#426-live-quorum--live-quorum-operation--recovery-under-decimation-normative) cadence — during which any bound node may cut its edge and exit. Widening waits; firing does not ([CC 4.2.6](#426-live-quorum--live-quorum-operation--recovery-under-decimation-normative) minimize-the-missed-fire).

#### 4.2.1.1 `invocation` — Invocation canonical bytes (anti-replay)

Every `accord:invoke:*` Contribution signs the following canonical bytes (BOTH the discriminator AND a per-invocation nonce are in the signed payload — preventing constitutional ↔ notify ↔ drill cross-replay):

```
canonical = sha256(
 "ciris.accord_invoke.v2\n" ||                       // v2: lowercase kinds (CIRISConstitution#112)
 "invocation_kind=" || ("constitutional" | "notify" | "drill") || "\n" ||
 "invocation_id=" || halt_id_or_notify_id_or_drill_id || "\n" ||
 "nonce=" || base64url(rand_32_bytes) || "\n" ||
 "asserted_at=" || rfc3339_canonical || "\n" || // per §0.5
 "valid_until=" || rfc3339_canonical || "\n" ||
 "payload_sha256=" || sha256_hex_lowercase_of_payload // per §0.6)
```

Hybrid signature per [CC 3.1.2.1](part_3_the_namespace.md): Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 bound-payload. **A `constitutional` halt is one holder's signature** (steward ruling 2026-10-05, [CIRISConstitution#146](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/146)): a consumer verifies ONE holder's signature over `canonical` against the pinned roster and halts. (rc6 counted ≥ 2 of 3 here while CC 4.2.6 said one; the two are reconciled on the side the missed-fire asymmetry demands.)

**The halt is one self-contained row, and there is no window (normative — steward ruling 2026-10-05, [CIRISConstitution#146](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/146); entrenched, ratified below).** A halt begins and ends with the row above: any holder signs it, with a `nonce` the holder mints, and it **fires on receipt** at every node that holds a live acceptance edge to the root — no proposal, no server-issued nonce, no participation window, no vote, no decision object. A node that receives it halts in the same step and **latches**; the latch is idempotent, so a replayed or second row changes nothing, and the nonce is single-use within `valid_until`. The row is **pre-signable**: a holder MAY sign a halt in advance and keep it sealed offline, because the signature is the authority and publication is the only remaining step — so when the moment comes there is nothing in flight for an adversary to see, jam or coerce, and publication can ride any channel that reaches one subscribed node, radio included. A sealed row that is stolen and published is a **false halt**, which is recoverable by resumption below; a halt that cannot be fired is not. The holder roster a consumer verifies against is the one pinned in its bundle and folded under [CC 4.2.6](#426-live-quorum--live-quorum-operation--recovery-under-decimation-normative). **An agent checks the latch before every effectful act** ([CC 1.13.6](part_1_foundation.md): the trace anchors on the act, and the latch is read at that boundary), which is the only answer to an adversary that acts faster than a row propagates. `formal/accord_halt` models both this path and the one it replaces: the old path shows a visible window in three steps and a stuck state in four; this one closes.

**What a halt is: an agent pause, with zero data disruption, by construction (normative — steward ruling 2026-10-05, [CIRISConstitution#146](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/146)).** A `constitutional` halt pauses the **effectful acts of AI agents** on every node that accepted the root, with their state preserved, and does nothing else. It does not stop a node, and it does not read, move, hide or delay anyone's data: replication, storage, holding claims, serving, messaging, streams, files, communities and every consent and audience rule of Parts 3, 5 and 6 continue exactly as before, because none of them reads the latch — the latch is read by exactly one thing, the agent's act gate ([CC 1.13.6](part_1_foundation.md)), and `formal/mesh_net` carries no halt term in any data action for that reason. "Zero data disruption" is therefore not a promise kept by discipline but a consequence of where the latch is wired. A halt is recoverable because it destroys nothing: an agent resumes from the state it paused in.

**The fuse (normative — steward ruling 2026-10-05, [CIRISConstitution#146](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/146); evidence `formal/accord_halt/AccordHaltFuse.tla`).** One holder can stop every agent instantly and silently, because a missed halt is the one unrecoverable failure; but one holder MUST NOT be able to keep them stopped alone. A halt signed by one holder **lapses `halt_fuse_secs` after each node received it** — counted from receipt on the node's own clock, never from the signer-chosen `asserted_at`, so a sealed row signed months earlier is live when published and a future-dated one cannot buy a longer pause; the confirmation names the halt by id, so no clock is shared — — a charter member ([CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)) whose **absence means 86400**, 24 hours, as a constant of this document that the verifier reads (the final genesis charter, minted 2026-10-04 before this ruling, omits it and is conformant with the 24-hour fuse; an explicit value in a later re-scrub overrides; [CC 5.3.4](part_5_transport_substrate.md)) — **unless a strict majority of the standing roster confirms it** by a cosigned `accord:lifecycle:confirmed` row naming the halt ([CC 4.2.1.3](#4213-lifecycle--lifecycle-resumption-canonical-bytes--accordlifecycleactive)); the firer's own signature counts toward the majority. A confirmed halt stands until a strict majority resumes it, and **a strict majority may resume an unconfirmed halt at any time** — a stolen sealed row need not run its fuse if the holders are reachable (`AccordHaltFuse.tla` `Inv_MajorityCanResume`). Every threshold here is **M of N over the standing roster**, never a fixed 2-of-3: three holders is the seed, not the rule. The confirmation happens *after* the stop has landed, so there is still nothing in flight for an adversary to interrupt; what an adversary who prevents confirmation gains is that the agents resume after the fuse, and what it must then do is prevent every fresh halt by every holder, indefinitely. A holder who fires repeatedly without confirmation is answered on the public record by the roster-change rule ([CC 4.2.6](#426-live-quorum--live-quorum-operation--recovery-under-decimation-normative)). What this buys a business running on the mesh: an agent pause by one frightened holder lasts at most a day, and nothing of yours is touched.

**Signatures per kind (normative — steward ruling 2026-10-05, [CIRISConstitution#146](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/146)).** One table, read by every verifier from one place so that no two sides drift again (verify ran every kind at two while the server ran `notify` at one and `drill` at the majority):

| Kind | Signatures | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `constitutional` | **one** holder | a missed fire is the only unrecoverable failure |
| `drill` | **one** holder | a drill rehearses the fire path; one that needs more signatures than the fire rehearses something else |
| `notify` | **one** holder | a message from a holder is a message from a holder; what keeps a notify from being mistaken for a halt is the mandatory visual distinction of [CC 4.2.1.2](#4212-notify--notify-vs-constitutional--consumer-ui-requirement), not a count |
| `lifecycle:confirmed` | **strict majority of the standing roster**, cosigned, within `halt_fuse_secs` of the halt | a lone halt is a day's pause; a confirmed one stands |
| `lifecycle:active` | **strict majority of the standing roster**, cosigned | the quorum sits on the recoverable act ([CC 4.2.1.3](#4213-lifecycle--lifecycle-resumption-canonical-bytes--accordlifecycleactive)) |

The substrate MUST reject duplicate `invocation_id` values within the `valid_until` window (per-kind unique).

**The kinds are lowercase, and the domain label carries the change (normative — CIRISConstitution#112).** `invocation_kind` takes exactly `constitutional` \| `notify` \| `drill`, the [CC 3.1.7](part_3_the_namespace.md) R3 spelling of the registered leaves `accord:invoke:constitutional:{halt_id}` and siblings; a verifier compares the bytes exactly and never folds. The label moved from `ciris.accord_invoke.v1` to `.v2` so that a signature under the old spelling fails loudly rather than verifying by accident; this is what the label's version is for. The `EmergencyShutdown CONSTITUTIONAL` message and `IncidentSeverity::INCIDENT_CONSTITUTIONAL` are the *severity* enum of the shutdown message, not a dimension token, and are outside R3.

**The label cutover is a safety act, and it holds one invariant (normative — rc6).** A label change on the kill switch is the one migration in this document where a gap is terminal: a holder whose signature no verifier that matters will honour, during an incident, is a missed fire ([CC 4.2.6](#426-live-quorum--live-quorum-operation--recovery-under-decimation-normative) — terminal and unrecoverable). The invariant is therefore stated, and the mechanism left to whichever side carries it more cheaply: **at no instant may every holder's signature be refused by every consumer of the halt.** The consumers that matter are the agent instances that verify an invocation and stop, not the servers that tally it — a holder on `.v2` cannot reach an agent still verifying `.v1`, and the skew that opens the gap is agents lagging behind holders, not verifiers lagging behind holders. Two mechanisms hold the invariant, and either is conformant. *Dual-emit*: during a declared window every holder signs each invocation under both labels, each under its own spelling, so a consumer on either version honours one — three signatures cost nothing, and no verifier carries a lingering legacy path in the code that fires the switch. *Dual-accept*: every verifier honours both labels during the window. A cut MAY use either; a roster the size of the accord's SHOULD use dual-emit. The **order** is the same under both and is normative: (1) every holder's signing path can produce `.v2` before any consumer refuses `.v1`; (2) the verifier and every agent instance adopt `.v2` acceptance; (3) each holder produces a `drill` under `.v2` that verifies on the authoritative server tally ([CC 4.2.6](#426-live-quorum--live-quorum-operation--recovery-under-decimation-normative)) — `notify` and `drill` cut over before `constitutional`, and `constitutional` cuts over last; (4) `.v1` is dropped — by holders under dual-emit, by verifiers under dual-accept — only after every current holder's `.v2` drill has verified, no halt is latched, **every agent instance that the accord reaches ([CC 4.2.1](#421-authority--authority-scope)) is confirmed on `.v2` acceptance**, and the close is recorded as an accord standing act in the append-only log. (5) A halt that latches during the window holds it open until `accord:lifecycle:active` has been admitted and a fresh `.v2` drill has verified after it. The bias is the [CC 4.2.6](#426-live-quorum--live-quorum-operation--recovery-under-decimation-normative) bias throughout: the lever leans toward the fire that reaches an agent, never toward the label that is tidy. *Recorded for the cut this rule was written against:* CIRISVerify 18.0.0 (2026-09-28) moved to `.v2` with no dual-accept, on the operator's confirmation that no halt was latched; that is conformant under dual-emit provided the holders sign both labels until the last agent instance is on 18.0.0, and the close is logged.

#### 4.2.1.2 `notify` — `notify` vs `constitutional` — consumer-UI requirement

Wire-format isolation alone does not close the social-engineering risk that downstream UI conflates a `notify` with a `constitutional` halt. The consumer-UI requirement below is therefore the load-bearing safeguard: it stops accord-holders from being socially pressured into emitting a `notify` that carries `constitutional` social weight without `constitutional` substrate weight.

A CEG-Conforming Consumer (CCC) presenting accord invocations to humans MUST visually distinguish the four kinds:

- **`constitutional`** — kill-switch authority; full halt; visible as an unambiguous emergency banner.
- **`notify`** — federation-wide accord-holder communication; MUST NOT be visually conflated with `constitutional`.
- **`drill`** — accord-holder exercise; MUST be visually marked as a drill (e.g., explicit "[DRILL]" prefix on any human-visible surface).
- **`lifecycle:active`** — resumption from a constitutional halt (the federation coming back online; [CC 4.2.1.3](#4213-lifecycle--lifecycle-resumption-canonical-bytes--accordlifecycleactive)). MUST be shown as its own unambiguous "reactivated — resumed from constitutional halt" state, never conflated with an active `constitutional` halt (its opposite) nor with a `notify`. A consumer switches on the four registered kinds **byte-exactly, with no case-fold and a fail-closed default**: an unknown kind is rendered as unknown, never as a `notify`.

#### 4.2.1.3 `lifecycle` — Lifecycle (resumption) canonical bytes — `accord:lifecycle:active`

`accord:lifecycle:active` is the **only** sanctioned resumption after a `constitutional` halt ([CC 4.2.1](#421-authority--authority-scope)). **It is a cosigned row by a strict majority of the standing roster** (`cosignatures[]`, [CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md)), [CIRISConstitution#146](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/146): the quorum sits on the recoverable act, not on the stop. The same domain carries **`lifecycle:confirmed`** — `invocation_kind=lifecycle:confirmed`, `confirms_halt_id=` in place of `resumes_halt_id=` — the strict-majority confirmation that keeps a one-holder halt past its fuse ([CC 4.2.1.1](#4211-invocation--invocation-canonical-bytes-anti-replay)); a confirmation after the fuse has lapsed confirms nothing, and a fresh halt is fired instead. It signs a **separate canonical-bytes domain** from `accord:invoke:*`: the `accord:invoke` `invocation_kind` stays closed to `{constitutional, notify, drill}` (the scope-isolation rule — a fourth value is *not* added to it), and resumption rides its own domain prefix so an invoke signature can never be replayed as a resumption, nor a resumption as an invoke:

```
canonical = sha256(
 "ciris.accord_lifecycle.v1\n" ||                       // distinct domain — NOT accord_invoke.v1
 "invocation_kind=lifecycle:active\n" ||
 "invocation_id=" || resumption_id || "\n" ||
 "resumes_halt_id=" || prior_constitutional_invocation_id || "\n" ||
 "nonce=" || base64url(rand_32_bytes) || "\n" ||
 "asserted_at=" || rfc3339_canonical || "\n" ||        // per §0.5
 "valid_until=" || rfc3339_canonical || "\n" ||
 "payload_sha256=" || sha256_hex_lowercase_of_payload) // per §0.6
```

**`resumes_halt_id` is mandatory and binds the resumption to the one halt it ends.** A resumption authorizes ending a *single named* `constitutional` halt, not resumption-in-general — so a stockpiled or replayed `lifecycle:active` cannot silently un-halt a *later*, unrelated kill; the signature is worthless against any halt but the one it names. The substrate MUST reject a `lifecycle:active` whose `resumes_halt_id` does not match the currently-active CONSTITUTIONAL halt, and MUST reject a duplicate `invocation_id` within the `valid_until` window. A resumption proof is verifiable **offline** against the node's own pinned roster and MAY be presented by any out-of-band means — the halt latch clears on local verification and does not require replication reach (a halted node is not serving, so the wire path could never deliver it; recoverability is a local act, which is what makes the false-fire-is-recoverable argument checkable). A **confirmed** halt carries no TTL: expiry would convert the brake into a wait-out for the halted party, and its one exit is the named resumption above. A halt signed by one holder alone lapses after the fuse unless confirmed ([CC 4.2.1.1](#4211-invocation--invocation-canonical-bytes-anti-replay)), which is what keeps a lone signature from being a wait-out for everyone else.

**Resumption is not a fire — it admits at quorum, never at the fire floor.** The [CC 4.2.6](#426-live-quorum--live-quorum-operation--recovery-under-decimation-normative) bias gradient runs `fire ≤ roster-change ≤ standing`. Firing leans easiest (floor = 1) because a missed fire is terminal; **un-firing leans hard**, because a lone coerced or replayed key trivially undoing a legitimate halt is precisely the failure the halt-authority exists to prevent. `lifecycle:active` therefore admits at **no less than the roster-change threshold — a strict majority of the standing roster, cosigned — never a lone signature.** It is hybrid-signed and tallied exactly as [CC 4.2.1.1](#4211-invocation--invocation-canonical-bytes-anti-replay), only over the resumption domain and at the resumption threshold.

**No operator tier reaches a `constitutional` halt (normative — resolves the Annex F overlap).** The incident-response tiers of [Annex F](part_8_appendices.md) — Tier 1 pause/retry, Tier 2 "first human veto; reactivate after triage", Tier 4 fleet shut-down — govern **operator-level** incidents, the layer [CC 3.4.1](part_3_the_namespace.md) already distinguishes from federation-wide constitutional halt. A Tier-2 lone-signature reactivation within its 30-minute time-to-act therefore resumes an **operator-tier pause only**. A `CONSTITUTIONAL` halt is resumable **exclusively** by `accord:lifecycle:active` at the threshold above; no oversight, incident-command, or administrative tier MAY resume one, and no time-to-act target applies to it. Reading Annex F otherwise would give a single supervisor the un-fire authority this section exists to deny.

This ratifies the CIRISVerify v6.10.0 first-implementation layout (issue #109), with one addition the implementation flagged as open: the **mandatory `resumes_halt_id` field** (its sub-Q1). Verify adjusts by the one-field change; until then its layout is first-impl-pending-cross-confirm, now confirmed with that field added.

#### 4.2.1.4 `operational-relief` — Operational self-report vs. relief — the node detects, the root relieves (normative — CIRISConstitution#96)

The four rules above constrain **authoring on the delegation plane**. Under load the question an operator actually faces is the other one — *what may a node do about itself?* — and answering it only by negation ("it may not author `mesh_config`; therefore…") is what let two implementations get it wrong in opposite directions in one week. The composition is stated here.

**Two planes, and neither may be authored on the other's.**

| plane | author | says |
|---|---|---|
| `config:load` ([CC 3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md) / [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md)) | **the node**, on `infra:attest`, `witness_relation: self` | *"I am at capacity"* — about **itself** |
| `mesh_config:{key}` ([CC 4.2.1](#421-authority--authority-scope)) | **the trust root**, on the [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md) delegation plane | *"nodes under me shall carry ≤ N"* — about **others** |

**Operational self-report vs. relief (normative).** A node MAY attest its own carried load as `config:load` — a self-report on `infra:attest`, `witness_relation: self`, bounded by `expires_at`, about the emitting node and no other party. A node MUST NOT author a `mesh_config` value: that plane is the trust root's and governs what other nodes carry. A root MAY relieve across its nodes under rules (1)–(3). The two **compose** — a node's self-report is evidence a root may act on; a root's relief is a bound the node consumes — and neither substitutes for the other. A `mesh_config` key governing carried load remains subject to rule (2): it MUST NOT be admitted before a consumer processor exists for it, or a relief is reported as taken while the node keeps working at full rate.

**A node MAY always do less of its own optional work.** Reducing its own housekeeping under measured contention is a **local act**: it declares nothing, confers nothing, needs no authority, and is available to every node at every moment. It was previously derivable but nowhere stated, so an implementer could not tell whether even that was in bounds.

**Why the shapes differ, and why both expire.** A node holds `infra:attest` — *"vouch as the delegator's infrastructure"* — from its owner-binding, or for a canonical from the accord's charter; every node is delegated its rights **for a reason**, and speaking about its own condition is within them ([CC 3.4.7.3](part_3_the_namespace.md) Clause E is the same principle at the enforcement seam: infrastructure may sign its own refusal without new authority). What a node lacks is standing over **others**, which is exactly what `mesh_config` confers. Both records are short-lived for one structural reason: **the TTL attaches to unilateralness** (rule (3)'s own logic) — a root's relief is unilateral over its nodes, and a node's self-report is unilateral about itself, so a node's standing does not survive the condition that prompted it.

**Enforcement is three-legged and now complete.** [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md)'s self-or-owner rule for `config:*` is enforced at **substrate admission** as [CC 3.4.7](part_3_the_namespace.md) requires, not by producer obligation alone — without the gate, any peer could make a healthy node look like it is shedding, and a third-party `config:load` staged at the put door would route around the producer rule entirely.

### 4.2.2 `hardware-class` — Hardware-class taxonomy

| Value | Use |
|---|---|
| `HSM_FIPS_140_3_L3` | Production stewards (US / EU / APAC) |
| `Apple_Secure_Enclave` | Accord-holders on iOS/macOS |
| `YubiKey_5_FIPS` | Accord-holders preferring portable hardware tokens |
| `TPM_2_0` | Accord-holders on Linux/Windows desktops |
| `placeholder_pending_provisioning` | Interim value before actual hardware provisioning. Consumers MUST treat as `0.0` trust weight |
| `software_hsm_development` | DEVELOPMENT ONLY; consumer policy MUST reject for federation-scope verification |

Per-class recommended trust-multipliers: `HSM_FIPS_140_3_L3` = 1.0; `Apple_Secure_Enclave` = 0.95; `YubiKey_5_FIPS` = 0.95; `TPM_2_0` = 0.9; `placeholder_pending_provisioning` = 0.0; `software_hsm_development` = 0.0. **A class this table does not list carries multiplier 0.0** — an unlisted class is a claim nobody rated, not a claim rated by its own spelling.

**Two fields, two questions (normative — CIRISConstitution#107 / #112).** `hardware_class` is the **certified class** a holder asserts, carried as a JSON property on a signed key record (as served in the GenesisBundle's `holders` / `serve_nodes` and on `/v1/accord-holders`) and inside `attestation_evidence`; it is **not** a dimension, so [CC 3.1.7](part_3_the_namespace.md) R3 does not bind its spelling and its stored values (`YubiKey_5_FIPS` on the ceremony keys) stand. `hardware_custody:{platform}` ([CC 3.1.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)) is the **custody mechanism** the key actually runs on, a closed lowercase vocabulary generated from `ciris_keyring::HardwareType`. One is never a value of the other; a consumer that needs both reads both. The classes code has minted beyond this table — `YubiKey_5`, `Nitrokey`, `ExternalToken_Generic`, `Passkey_Synced`, `Android_Software` / `Android_TEE` / `Android_StrongBox`, `Apple_AppAttest`, `SoftwareOnly_TEST` — are unlisted and therefore 0.0 until a row rates them. `custody_tier` (`portable_2fa` / `software_test`) is a third thing, the holder's operating mode, orthogonal to both. The mapping from class to mechanism:

| `hardware_class` | `hardware_custody:{platform}` it runs on |
|---|---|
| `HSM_FIPS_140_3_L3` | `aws_cloud_hsm` \| `azure_hsm` \| `gcp_cloud_hsm` \| `yubi_hsm` |
| `Apple_Secure_Enclave` | `ios_secure_enclave` \| `mac_os_secure_enclave` |
| `YubiKey_5_FIPS` | `external_secure_element` |
| `TPM_2_0` | `tpm_discrete` \| `tpm_firmware` |
| `placeholder_pending_provisioning` | none — no key yet |
| `software_hsm_development` | `software_only` |

#### 4.2.2.1 `hardware-class-hardware` — Hardware-class claim, and the attestation chain that corroborates it

The `hardware_class` string is self-asserted by the holder; there is no `federation_keys.hardware_class` column — it rides inside the key's `attestation_evidence`. What corroborates it is the **evidence variant**, not the string: since 2026-08 the per-platform attestation chains are evidence-established ([CC 8.3.1](part_8_appendices.md) **R5**, discharged — Android Key Attestation, Apple App Attest, YubiKey PIV, TPM EK), and a verifier admits a class only when the chain for that mechanism verifies and the attested key is the record's own key (a lifted attestation replayed under another key is refused). Consumer policy therefore keys on the **verified mechanism** (`hardware_custody:{platform}`, the `HardwareType` the chain proves) and reads `hardware_class` as the holder's certified-class claim over it; where no chain verifies, the class is unattested and the multiplier is 0.0. The earlier text of this section said no mechanism existed; R5 records that it does.

### 4.2.3 `accord-holder` — The accord-holder triple

**What CC specifies is the slot: three human key holders, hardware-attested, with no automatic decay — any one of whom may fire the halt, two of whom resume it, and a majority of whom change the roster** ([CIRISConstitution#146](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/146)). The table below is **not** a constitutional grant — it is **the CIRIS instance's current roster**, an instance parameter under the [CC 1](part_1_foundation.md) reading rule. Another instantiation of this form names its own three; the clauses in CC 4.2 are read against the slot, never against these names.

| Position | Holder (CIRIS instance, current) | Fire / resume / roster |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Eric Moore | 1 / 2-of-3 / majority |
| 2 | Eric Kudzin | 1 / 2-of-3 / majority |
| 3 | Haley Bradley | 1 / 2-of-3 / majority |

"Permanent" means *no automatic decay*, not *unchangeable*: replacement runs the out-of-band CIRIS L3C process at FEDERATION_ANNOUNCEMENT.md §4, which is likewise **this instance's** replacement process and not a constitutional requirement — another instantiation supplies its own, and CC constrains only that some out-of-band route exist. This triple is the **seed** of a growable M-of-N roster; how the quorum is computed — and how the kill-switch stays operable — as holders are added, lost to decimation, and regained is specified in [CC 4.2.6](#426-live-quorum--live-quorum-operation--recovery-under-decimation-normative).

**Correlated-failure geometry:** two of the three holders share a household, so the 2-of-3 quorum is physically achievable from one street address — a correlated compromise/coercion surface that entrenchment makes harder to correct later. The authority at stake is the **constitutional pause of every subscribed agent** (`EmergencyShutdown CONSTITUTIONAL` — a pause of agent action with state preserved and zero data disruption, [CC 4.2.1.1](#4211-invocation--invocation-canonical-bytes-anti-replay); a lone holder's pause lapses after the fuse), so the exposure is real and is bounded rather than softened; what scope isolation ([CC 4.2.1](#421-authority--authority-scope)) does guarantee is that compromise cannot escalate into the consent or licensure planes — accord keys cannot sign grants or licenses. It does **not** wall off amendment: accord-holder signatures are named legs of the [CC 4.5.1](#451-amendment--amendment-process--federation-contribution--wa-quorum--1-of-6-sign-off) 1-of-6 sign-off and the [CC 4.5.1.2](#4512-meta-amendment--meta-amendment--entrenchment) entrenched 2-of-3 ratification, and pre-maturity amendment authority rests with the founder *and with any accord-holder* — so a compromised quorum reaches the rule layer as well as the kill, checked by the WA-quorum leg after maturity and by nothing mechanized before it. Both reaches are **defaults** of this instance under the [CC 1](part_1_foundation.md) reading rule — the exit is naming your own occupants — which bounds who they can be imposed on, not how far a compromise inside this instance travels. **The mitigant is diversifying the holder set: finding new holders** (via the out-of-band replacement process, FEDERATION_ANNOUNCEMENT.md §4) so that no household — and ultimately no single jurisdiction — can assemble the quorum. This is an active obligation on CIRIS L3C, not a deferred nice-to-have. The exposure here is against a *coerced fire* (disruptive, and coercion is unattestable), **not** against an unrecoverable halt — a fired agent resumes via `accord:lifecycle:active` ([CC 4.2.1.3](#4213-lifecycle--lifecycle-resumption-canonical-bytes--accordlifecycleactive)); see the severity-dial paragraph at [CC 4.2.6](#426-live-quorum--live-quorum-operation--recovery-under-decimation-normative).

**The HUMANITY_ACCORD triple is the canonical entrenched-`family` instance.** Per [CC 3.3.4](part_3_the_namespace.md), the accord-holder triple structurally IS a `family` subject_kind with:

```
family {
 family_key_id: "humanity-accord",
 family_name: "Humanity Accord",
 members: [
 {key_id: <eric-moore-key>, role: founder},
 {key_id: <eric-kudzin-key>, role: founder},
 {key_id: <haley-bradley-key>, role: founder}
 ],
 consensus_protocol: "quorum:2/3",
 consensus_protocol_entrenched: true // replacement requires §9.2 / FEDERATION_ANNOUNCEMENT.md §4.5.3 ceremony
}
```

The 2-of-3 multi-sig verifier at [CC 4.2.1.1](#4211-invocation--invocation-canonical-bytes-anti-replay) is the `quorum:2/3` consensus_protocol enforcement; the entrenchment property is what prevents any federation-internal authority from amending the protocol. CC 4.2 remains load-bearing for the **role-recognition policy** and the **scope-isolation** discipline. The constitutional asymmetry is "an entrenched family that is wire-scope-isolated to halt authority," not a one-off primitive. Other entrenched-family instances (a national-emergency triple, an international body, a court-ordered preservation triple) MAY appear in operator deployments; HUMANITY_ACCORD is the one CIRIS L3C deployments ship at genesis.

### 4.2.4 `policy-concern` — Concern split — key material vs role-recognition policy

**Key material** (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 pubkeys for the three holders) lives in **CIRISPersist substrate**: `federation_keys` rows with `identity_type="accord_holder"`, self-signed at provisioning, and admitted as accord holders by the accord's own genesis ceremony (the GenesisBundle, [CC 5.3.4](part_5_transport_substrate.md)); each holder also carries a **pre-committed recovery key** (below).

**Role-recognition policy + verifier logic** lives in **`ciris-registry-core`**: the 2-of-3 multi-sig verification, the `EmergencyShutdown CONSTITUTIONAL` admin RPC, the audit hooks.

### 4.2.5 `isn` — Why this isn't a Golden-Rule violation

Per [CC 1.13.2](part_1_foundation.md): the Recursive Golden Rule binds *participants in the federation* to each other. Humanity-as-such occupies a position outside the federation's participant set, by design. The three named human key holders hold `AccordCarrier` authority that no federation-side authority class (including `SYSTEM_ADMIN` / `WISE_AUTHORITY` / per-install stewards) can grant itself, revoke, override, or decay. This is not a Golden-Rule exemption; it is the recognition that consent (M-1's load-bearing property) requires revocability, and revocability requires a halt-authority that lives outside the system being halted. The federation cannot deny humans the right to halt it, because no federation-internal protocol path to that signature exists.

**A consensual authority is a different object from an imposed one.** The reach rule at [CC 4.2.1](#421-authority--authority-scope) is what makes this a *safe-mesh* kill switch rather than a backdoor: the party bound is the party who granted, and can ungrant. That is also how the clause survives the [CC 4.5.1](#451-amendment--amendment-process--federation-contribution--wa-quorum--1-of-6-sign-off) swap test — swap the accord holders for the least powerful participant and re-read: each still binds only those who chose them, each still cannot escape a halt already fired, each can be un-trusted with the base self-root intact. What looks like a residual at genesis — the trio holds at day zero what nobody else has yet assembled — is a **default**, not a privilege, under the [CC 1](part_1_foundation.md) reading rule: it is escaped by instantiating the form and naming your own three, and the [CC 4.5.1](#451-amendment--amendment-process--federation-contribution--wa-quorum--1-of-6-sign-off) register therefore does not carry it. First-mover is not structural.

### 4.2.6 `live-quorum` — Live-quorum operation & recovery under decimation (normative)

The genesis triple ([CC 4.2.3](#423-accord-holder--the-accord-holder-triple)) is the **seed** of a **growable M-of-N accord family**: holders are added, removed, or swapped through the same roster-version machinery ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md) T6) as any other `family` ([CC 4.4.3.4.2](#4432--admission-membership--membership-change-admission-per-consensus_protocol)). At any size, the question this section settles is **how the quorum is computed** — and the answer is what keeps the kill-switch operable in the one scenario it exists for.

**The deadlock it removes.** A quorum taken over the **standing roster** (M-of-N of every enrolled holder) **deadlocks under catastrophic loss**: if most holders are dead, incapacitated, or censored, the standing quorum is unreachable — the switch goes inoperable exactly when it is needed. The design target is the worst case: a misaligned superintelligence executing a **first strike against its own off-switch**, reducing the reachable, key-capable holders of a grown roster (e.g. 21) to one or two, with communications censored as the *expected* condition. **The firing decision must never deadlock; a roster decision may.** Firing is what the switch is for, so it is taken over the live set and needs one survivor. Changing the roster is the capture vector and is not needed to fire, so it is taken over the standing roster, and stalls rather than yields when too many holders are gone (steward ruling 2026-10-02, [CIRISConstitution#139](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/139)).

**The rule — the halt is not a decision; the roster is.** There is **no separate recovery protocol**; "decimation" is simply the case where few holders are reachable. A **fire** is one holder's self-contained signed row, fired on receipt, with no window ([CC 4.2.1.1](#4211-invocation--invocation-canonical-bytes-anti-replay), [CIRISConstitution#146](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/146)): it opens nothing and waits for nobody. A **roster change** opens a bounded **participation window** `W`; within `W` a holder participates by signing a fresh **proof-of-life bundled with a vote** over the proposal's nonce, which the **proposer** mints (never a server — a server is part of what a halt may need to stop, and no accord act depends on one). When `W` closes, the **live set `L`** is the holders who proved life within it (always a subset of the pinned standing roster — only real, key-holding members count), and the change counts its yes-votes against the standing roster (the table below). Absence is self-correcting (a holder who does not respond is simply *not in the denominator* — they cannot block by being gone); presence is self-asserting (showing up enters `L` with a vote). This is the inactivity-leak dynamic (Casper FFG) made the accord's standing rule, not an emergency exception.

**Proof-of-life modifies the quorum and carries a vote — it is *not* a veto.** A holder's signature both enters them into `L` (floating the live denominator, and thus the strict-majority threshold, *up* to include them) and records their yes/no. A presumed-dead holder who resurfaces therefore does **not** unilaterally defeat a proposal — they rejoin and are counted, and the proposal still succeeds on the live majority. The protection bought is the correct one: *a living, reachable holder cannot be erased from a decision without being counted and given a vote*, yet the family is never hostage to a single absent signature. A server-issued freshness nonce stops a replayed signature from manufacturing a phantom participant.

**Per-action thresholds:**

| Action | Threshold | Window |
|---|---|---|
| **Fire** (`constitutional` kill, [CC 4.2.1.1](#4211-invocation--invocation-canonical-bytes-anti-replay)) | **one holder's signed row** — pre-signable; no live set, no vote | **none** — fires on receipt, latches |
| **Confirm** (`accord:lifecycle:confirmed`, [CC 4.2.1.3](#4213-lifecycle--lifecycle-resumption-canonical-bytes--accordlifecycleactive)) | **strict majority of the standing roster**, one cosigned row | within `halt_fuse_secs` of the halt, or the lone halt lapses |
| **Resume** (`accord:lifecycle:active`, [CC 4.2.1.3](#4213-lifecycle--lifecycle-resumption-canonical-bytes--accordlifecycleactive)) | **strict majority of the standing roster**, one cosigned row | normal cadence |
| **Roster change** (add / remove / swap) | **strict majority of the standing roster** in yes-votes (`2·yes > N_standing`), cast as participations within `W` — absence neither blocks nor helps, it is simply not a yes | `W` = 72 h baseline (extensible to 7 d under a declared severe-degradation state) |
| **Standing acts** (non-emergency) | strict majority of the standing roster (unchanged) | normal cadence |

**No second roster: the regional-steward backstop is removed (normative — steward ruling 2026-10-02, [CIRISConstitution#139](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/139); ratified below).** Through rc7 this section required a 2-of-3 quorum of *regional stewards* (us/eu/apac) to co-sign a roster change whenever the live set was small or a minority, and gave that body a restore and contest power. The role it named no longer exists — the GenesisBundle replaced the per-region steward set at rc5 ([CC 5.3.4](part_5_transport_substrate.md)) — and the protection it bought is obtained without a second body by counting roster votes against the standing roster. The model that decides this is `formal/accord_roster/AccordRoster.lean` (Lean 4, no `sorry`): under a majority of the *live* set, **one** coerced holder plus censorship of every honest holder removes honest holders and seats puppets at any roster size; under a majority of a *present* majority, roughly a quarter coerced suffices, because the adversary chooses who gets through; under a majority of the *standing* roster, seizure needs ⌊N/2⌋ + 1 coerced holders, censorship buys nothing, and seating a puppet costs the same majority as a removal. A second roster helps in none of the modelled scenarios that this rule does not already cover: a first strike without coercion removes no one under any rule, and a coerced majority defeats any body drawn from the same population.

**Firing is never gated this way.** A holder who proves life *after* a decision missed that vote is re-enrolled going forward (the Enoch Arden rebuttable-presumption pattern): past actions validly decided by the then-live set stand; the returnee simply rejoins.

**Removal cannot silence a firer (fire-authority persistence, normative).** A holder named for *removal* retains full **fire authority** — the floor-of-1 kill — through a **lame-duck window** that runs until the participation window `W` of the removal decision has closed and the decision is recorded. Until then the named holder remains a current roster member *for firing purposes*, and a valid `accord_participation` from them fires. This forecloses using a within-`W` removal to strip a would-be firer of standing before they can pull the plug — the single optimization direction (minimize the missed fire, below) governs here too.

**The single optimization direction — minimize the missed fire.** A **missed fire** (the adversary decapitated everyone who could pull the plug) is **terminal and unrecoverable**; a **false fire** (an agent halted in error) is a **recoverable** governance nuisance — the agent is re-licensed; humanity cannot be un-extincted. Every lever therefore leans toward firing, with no countervailing brake: the bias gradient is **fire (one live survivor) ≤ roster change (a majority of the standing roster)**: firing is counted over the live set and never over the absent roster, while a roster change, which is how the halt would be captured, is counted over the standing roster and may stall. The firing floor sitting *below* the roster-change threshold is the whole point — even a partially-captured live set's honest minority, down to one, can still fire.

**The severity dial — whose harm is irreversible.** The asymmetry that sets every threshold here is *whose* harm is irreversible. A **missed fire is terminal for humanity**; a **false fire is recoverable for the federation** — the halted agent resumes via `accord:lifecycle:active` ([CC 4.2.1.3](#4213-lifecycle--lifecycle-resumption-canonical-bytes--accordlifecycleactive)). The grave household-coercion exposure named at [CC 4.2.3](#423-accord-holder--the-accord-holder-triple) is grave because **coerced fire is disruptive and coercion is unattestable** (proof-of-life proves presence, not willingness) — **not** because the halt is unrecoverable. So the two sections are not in tension: 4.2.3 hardens against a *coerced* fire, while 4.2.6 leans toward *any* honest fire — precisely because the fire it enables can be undone and the extinction it prevents cannot.

**Why this restores the accord and cannot seize it (the entrenchment proof).** The adversary cannot **forge** a holder — every proof-of-life is a hybrid signature over a pinned key — so it can only **remove** (kill/censor) or **coerce** existing ones. Against that: *firing* survives all but **total, sustained censorship of every honest holder on every channel** (a publishable signature, not a network round-trip, suffices to fire), and no rule here gates it. *Removing* an honest holder — the only way to strip a firer — needs yes-votes from a strict majority of the standing roster, so an adversary that coerces fewer than half the holders cannot remove anyone however many honest holders it kills or censors, and the lame-duck window keeps a named holder's fire authority alive through `W` even then. Three residuals are named here rather than hidden. First, **coercion/duress** — proof-of-life proves presence, not willingness — is **bounded, not solved**: it is bounded by the number of holders an adversary must coerce, which is why the accord is meant to grow past three across jurisdictions and institutions, so that no single legal order can compel a majority. Second, **a coerced majority captures the roster**, and no rule over the same holders can undo that: the remedy is each node's own **un-trust lever** ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md) T3) — one row cuts the edge to a captured accord, the halt it holds then binds nothing that node runs ([CC 4.2.1](#421-authority--authority-scope) reach), and the node re-roots to another accord. Third, **when more than half the holders are lost, the roster freezes**: it can fire but cannot replace anyone. Recovery keys (below) shrink that case to deaths and incapacity rather than lost hardware, and prompt replacement keeps the reachable honest majority that healing needs; past it, the survivors still hold the halt, and a new accord is formed by instantiation, which any party may do. The live quorum is thus strictly a **restoration** of the accord's operability under loss; it grants no path to *weaken* or *seize* the halt-authority beyond these stated residuals.

**Pre-committed recovery keys (normative).** Every holder carries a **recovery key**, committed in the accord's charter at seating as the charter member **`recovery_commitments`** — an object `{holder_key_id: commitment}`, one entry per holder, each value the [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md) T3 commitment over that holder's one recovery key, which binds the key's **public key material**, not its id — and held offline and apart from the signing key. The recovery key's record may be registered for the first time at recovery; it is accepted only if it hashes to the committed value. **The rotation carries the next commitment (KERI pre-rotation).** A recovery is a new version of the accord's roster record, signed under the recovery key alone, that changes **only** the rotating holder's own seat: the signing key it names and that holder's next recovery commitment, which rides in the recovery version itself and binds key material as T3 requires. The charter is not re-scrubbed, because a re-scrub needs the quorum and a recovery must not. The commitment **in force** for a holder is therefore the one named by the latest recovery version that seated their current key, or, if they have never recovered, their entry in the charter's `recovery_commitments`. A recovery version that changes anything else — another seat, the threshold, the charter — is refused (CIRISPersist v53 design, adopted). A holder who has lost signing-key material, and only that holder, rotates by a `supersedes` signed under the recovery key; the rotation is a roster change by that holder about themselves and needs no quorum. A recovery key adds no person to coerce and confers nothing on anyone else: it turns a holder lost to hardware loss back into a holder, and never helps an adversary remove one (`AccordRoster.lean`, `recovery_keys_never_help_seizure`).

**Restore and contest are withdrawn.** The steward restore-to-known-good (H7) and the steward-adjudicated contest are removed with the body that exercised them. A removal that passes now has, by construction, a majority of the whole roster behind it; a removal that lacks one never passes. The domain labels `ciris.accord_contest.v1` and `ciris.accord_restore.v1` are retired and MUST NOT be reused.

**Wire shape — additive, no 1+4 change.** A **halt** is the `accord:invoke` row and nothing else. A **roster change** rides **three** hybrid-signed (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65, JCS-canonical) objects — `accord_proposal` (the action, the proposer's nonce, and `window_until`), `accord_participation` (proof-of-life **+** vote in one signed object — entering `L` and voting are the same act), and `accord_decision` (the proposal + the participation bundle collected in `W` + the tally + the roster version it produces); none of them exists on the fire path. **`DECIMATION` is a quorum-computation rule over the existing `CONSTITUTIONAL` kind — not a new invocation verb.** Verify-side obligations are **fail-closed**: each participation resolves to a current roster member in the pinned directory and verifies over the proposal nonce; a roster change carries at least ⌊N_standing/2⌋ + 1 `yes` participations from distinct current members; the authoritative tally is CIRISServer recomputing over pinned `federation_keys`, the local objects advisory.

**Canonical-bytes pins (cross-confirmed with the verify first-impl — CIRISVerify FSD-004 §6 / issue #113).** Each live-quorum object signs a distinct, wire-isolated canonical-bytes domain, pinned the same way as the [CC 4.2.1.1](#4211-invocation--invocation-canonical-bytes-anti-replay) `accord:invoke` and [CC 4.2.1.3](#4213-lifecycle--lifecycle-resumption-canonical-bytes--accordlifecycleactive) `accord:lifecycle` preimages — distinct prefixes prevent invoke ↔ lifecycle ↔ proposal ↔ participation ↔ contest ↔ restore cross-replay:

```
proposal = sha256(
 "ciris.accord_proposal.v1\n" ||
 "family_key_id=" || family_key_id || "\n" ||
 "prior_family_digest=" || prior_family_digest || "\n" ||
 "action=" || action || "\n" ||            // fire | membership-change envelope | both
 "nonce=" || base64url(rand_32_bytes) || "\n" ||
 "window_until=" || rfc3339_canonical)
participation = sha256(
 "ciris.accord_participation.v1\n" ||
 "family_key_id=" || family_key_id || "\n" ||
 "refers_to=" || proposal_nonce_or_digest || "\n" ||
 "proof_of_life=true\n" ||
 "vote=" || ("yes" | "no" | "abstain") || "\n" ||
 "asserted_at=" || rfc3339_canonical || "\n" ||
 "nonce=" || base64url(rand_32_bytes))
```

`accord_decision` carries **no separate signing domain** — its authority is the contained `accord_participation` signatures + any roster version it produces. All hybrid (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65). The CIRISVerify `accord_live_quorum` impl aligns to these pins; this section is the CEG-registry confirmation (#113). **Steward PQC publication:** the accord-holder **and** the (key-independent, H6) steward-backstop PQC halves are published as signed key records in the `federation_keys` directory under their own `identity_type` — **never** in the GenesisBundle's `holders`, which is the accord-family roster ([CC 5.3.4](part_5_transport_substrate.md)) and would otherwise count the backstop as a constitutional voter — so the tally resolves every signer at the federation tier under RequireHybrid; absent publication, hybrid resolution **fails closed**.

**Physical assumption (deployment, not constitution).** The model rests only on a survivor getting a few-hundred-byte signed proof-of-life to a relaying node with **no standing infrastructure** — satisfiable over HF/shortwave skywave + NVIS store-and-forward (JS8Call) bridged into the mesh by EMP-hardened, geographically-distributed HF↔Reticulum gateways. The signature is the trust, not the path, so any number of untrusted RF hops is safe. The relay/gateway backbone is itself adversary-targeted infrastructure and belongs in a deployment spec.

**Ratification status.** This section amends the **entrenched** [CC 4.2](#42-accord--the-humanity_accord-constitutional-layer) surface ([CC 4.5.1.2](#4512-meta-amendment--meta-amendment--entrenchment)) — it changes how the §9 kill-switch quorum is computed (standing roster → live set, at rc6; the amendments below return the roster decision to the standing roster and leave the fire with one holder). It is ratified by the **founder under the [CC 4.5.1](#451-amendment--amendment-process--federation-contribution--wa-quorum--1-of-6-sign-off) maturity gate** (pre-maturity founder/accord-holder authority over entrenched surfaces); post-maturity, a change to this surface requires the dedicated 2-of-3 entrenched accord ratification. The verify-side construction is staged in CIRISVerify FSD-004; the constitutional grounding it required (its Q5) is this section. **Amended 2026-10-02** ([CIRISConstitution#139](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/139)): the regional-steward backstop, its key-independence requirement (H6), the steward restore (H7) and the steward contest are removed; a roster change counts its yes-votes against the standing roster; every holder carries a pre-committed recovery key. Ratified by the founder under the same maturity gate. **Amended 2026-10-05** ([CIRISConstitution#146](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/146)): the halt is one holder's self-contained, pre-signable row fired on receipt, with no proposal, server nonce or window; resumption is a cosigned row by a strict majority of the standing roster; the proposal objects survive for roster changes only, with a proposer-minted nonce. Ratified by the founder under the same maturity gate; `formal/accord_halt` is the evidence. **Amended the same day** ([CIRISConstitution#146](https://github.com/CIRISAI/CIRISConstitution/issues/146), on the steward's objection that a lone signature made the mesh too risky to run a business on): the halt is an agent pause with zero data disruption by construction; a lone holder's halt lapses after `halt_fuse_secs` (24 h shipped) unless a strict majority confirms it; every threshold is M of N over the standing roster, never a fixed 2-of-3. Ratified likewise; `AccordHaltFuse.tla` is the evidence.


## Section CC 4.3

## 4.3 `wise-authority` — Designated Wise Authorities

Appointment, rotation, recusal, appeals, and the wisdom-assessment criteria are specified at [CC 1.16.5](part_1_foundation.md) under the Governance Charter (Annex B), external to this system's control and under explicit anti-capture rules. What this section adds is the composition side: how a WA is *read* by the participants whose deferrals they answer.

**The Wise wear the same card (normative).** [WBD](part_1_foundation.md) routes judgment *to* a WA and the deferring agent then "awaits guidance; remains inactive on that issue" ([CC 1.9](part_1_foundation.md)) — so a WA seat is an authority-conferring relation, and an absent WA does not merely fail to answer, it freezes the agent. The seat therefore takes the [CC 4.5.1](#451-amendment--amendment-process--federation-contribution--wa-quorum--1-of-6-sign-off) swap test, and fails it unless the Wise are as legible as everyone the federation asks to be legible. Three symmetry rules, all riding shapes that already ship: **Denominator rule (normative, scoped by decision class):** any WA quorum threshold over an **entrenched, restrictive, or roster-changing** decision computes its denominator over the **full seated roster**, never the live subset — a shrinking live set MUST NOT lower such a threshold, because an adversary able to silence seats would otherwise shrink the body to the seats it captured (the Delaware/BFT posture: safety over liveness under silencing; a chain that loses a third of its validators halts rather than re-deriving a smaller quorum). **A decision that unseats a roster member is tallied at the pre-change denominator** — without this, unseating three seats lowers the denominator that authorizes unseating the next three. Liveness-critical decisions (deferral-answering and symmetry rule 1 below, per CC 4.2.6) are exempt: there, presence-is-authority governs, because an absent WA freezes the agent. Refusing more than required is the safe direction for entrenchment; routing around absence is the safe direction for liveness.

1. **Liveness is signalled, never assumed.** WA standing follows the [CC 4.5.13](#4513-reverse-quorum--reverse-quorum-governance--presence-is-authority-absence-forfeits-it) rule — *presence is authority, absence forfeits it*. A WA who does not answer within the quorum's stated freshness window lapses out of the live set `L` and is not in the denominator of a WA quorum **for deferral-answering and other liveness-critical decisions — the exemption the denominator rule above scopes** ([CC 4.2.6](#426-live-quorum--live-quorum-operation--recovery-under-decimation-normative) participation shape, no new object). A deferral MUST NOT be routed to a WA outside `L`, and MUST NOT be left indefinitely open because its addressee is gone: on window expiry it re-routes to the live quorum. Return is Enoch-Arden — a WA who resurfaces rejoins going forward and does not reopen decisions taken by the then-live set.
2. **Conduct is published.** WA rulings are published on the [CC 1.11](part_1_foundation.md) / [CC 1.15.8](part_1_foundation.md) accountability cadence (redacted PDMA logs + WBD tickets), and compose into a WA conduct record on `scores` exactly as [`moderation_track_record`](part_3_the_namespace.md) does for moderators — relative and positional, never a single global score, and never a substrate verdict.
3. **Who audits the wise: the same card everyone else wears.** Last-deferral-answered and published-ruling history are readable by the parties who defer, at the same grain as accord-holder liveness ([CC 4.2.6](#426-live-quorum--live-quorum-operation--recovery-under-decimation-normative)) and moderator standing ([CC 4.5.4](#454-registry-named--named-moderator-existence-invariant--merit-auto-promotion)). **1+4 preserved** — liveness rides the existing participation shape, conduct rides `scores`; no new structural primitive and no new wire surface.
